title: Ignatiana: A Research Apparatus for Ignatian Spirituality
description:
A research apparatus for Ignatian spirituality, confined to the old Society (1540–1773) and organised in five lines: the founder's own writings (the Spiritual Exercises in a trilingual public-domain parallel edition — Spanish Autograph, Vulgata of 1548, Mullan 1914 — and the letters of 1524–1547 in full); the school of discernment (the Official Directory of 1599 and Favre's Memoriale, both bilingual); the Society in the world; Friedrich Spee; and the counter-voices. With a canonical paragraph-level citation index, a cross-corpus concordance, a concept atlas, curated reading paths, a discernment lexicon, registers of persons and places, and a citation-bound dialogue with the corpus.

Four modern translations (Ganss, Padberg, Divarkar, Munitiz) remain in copyright: their structure, statistics and citation anchors are part of the apparatus, but no text of them is distributed — a reader opens them from a copy they own, on their own device.
